title: 6.8.12 Plain English to Pseudocode: The Slingshot
description: Turn the plain-English rules of a slingshot into pseudocode: grab, stretch and release, guarded by one variable, with the force applied in exactly one frame.

steps.title: Turn the plain-English steps into pseudocode
steps.instructions:
Here is the plan in plain English:

**1.** Each frame, ask three questions in a row.

**2.** Grab: if the mouse was just pressed while over the ball, the ball is now held.

**3.** Stretch: if the ball is held and the mouse is still down, move the ball to the mouse and draw the band.

**4.** Release: if the ball is held and the mouse was let go, work out the force, apply it to the ball, and the ball is no longer held.

**5.** If nothing is being done to the ball (idle), all three answers are no and the frame just ends.

The same plan is drawn as a flow chart above the editor. You do not draw it, you read it: follow the arrows and match each box to one of the steps.

In `README.md`, type these as numbered pseudocode **between the first and last line**. Write three separate IF blocks, one per question, each closed with END IF. Name the variable `held` and the two calls `drawBand` and `applyForce`. Number every line, including the indented ones and the END IF lines. Each keyword looks like this, in a different program:

- `IF key is pressed AND player is grounded` ... `END IF` (a question the frame asks)
- `SET jumping TO true` (a change; use `false` to turn something off)
- `CALL playSound` (call another function)
- `SET player position TO the spawn point` (move something)

The force is applied on exactly **one** frame of the whole throw. If you put it on the stretch path, the ball would speed up every frame you hold it.

Plain English is fine here. Press **Grade** above the editor: the AI reads what your steps mean and marks each Quest card green or red. Changing your text clears its marks, so press Grade again when you have finished editing.
hints: `held` guards both the stretch and the release. Without it, the release would fire whether or not anything had been picked up.
The force belongs in exactly one block.

requirements.title: Ten or more numbered steps
requirements.description: Number every line 1. 2. 3. and so on, with something written after each number.
requirements.hint: You need at least ten lines that start with a number, one after another. Number the indented lines and the END IF lines too.

requirements.title: Grab: pressing on the ball marks it held
requirements.description: When the mouse is pressed on the ball, held becomes true.
requirements.hint: Grab: when the mouse is pressed on the ball, mark it as held.

requirements.title: Stretch: while held and the mouse is down, the ball follows and the band is drawn
requirements.description: A question guarded by held, with the ball moved to the mouse and the band drawn inside it.
requirements.hint: Stretch: only while the ball is held and the mouse is down, move the ball to the mouse and draw the band.

requirements.title: Release: while held, letting go launches the ball and clears held
requirements.description: A question guarded by held, with the force applied and held cleared inside it.
requirements.hint: Release: only while the ball is held and the mouse is let go, apply the force and clear held.

requirements.title: The launch happens once
requirements.description: The force is applied in one place only. A force every frame is the classic physics bug.
requirements.hint: Apply the force exactly once, in the release block. Not on the stretch path.

requirements.title: Three questions, each closed
requirements.description: Three IF blocks, each closed with END IF.
requirements.hint: Write three IF blocks, each closed with END IF. Do not write GO TO or LOOP BACK.

planChart.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A([draw runs]) --> B{pressed on the ball?}
  B -- yes --> C[the ball is held]
  C --> D{held and mouse down?}
  B -- no --> D
  D -- yes --> E[move the ball to the mouse]
  E --> F[[draw the band]]
  F --> G{held and mouse let go?}
  D -- no --> G
  G -- yes --> H[work out the force]
  H --> I[[launch the ball]]
  I --> J[the ball is no longer held]
  J --> Z([end of frame])
  G -- no --> Z
